title: Recording: You Can’t Catch Me by John Lennon | 1974
content:
Record Plant, New York City
Producer: John Lennon

John Lennon began the New York sessions for his Rock ‘N’ Roll album on 9 July 1974.

Much of the album had been recorded in Los Angeles the previous year with Phil Spector producing, but Spector had disappeared with the tapes for some months. With the assistance of Capitol Records’ vide president Al Coury, Lennon recovered the tapes and was able to produce new sessions to complete the album.

Twenty-four boxes of tapes arrived in New York City on this day, and Lennon spent several hours reviewing the audio at the Record Plant. He also overdubbed fresh vocals onto ‘You Can’t Catch Me’, the backing track for which was recorded on 11 December 1973, and taped some messages for the producers of the forthcoming stage show John, Paul, George, Ringo… & Bert.
